newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Afghan refugees in Turkmenistan gone home - UN.
newsitem.headline: Afghan refugees in Turkmenistan gone home - UN.

text.p: Some 8,000 Afghans who fled to Turkmenistan last week to escape fighting between rival factions in their own country have returned home, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Friday.

A UNHCR spokeswoman told Reuters the refugees -- all but about 140 young men -- had crossed back into Afghanistan after an official of the agency had gone to the Afghan town of Mari Chak to ensure that checked that all fighting there had ceased.

Citing information telephoned from the scene by UNHCR field officers to the agency's Geneva headquarters, she said the return movement had begun on Thursday night after the refugees had been provided with food, and was over on Friday.

The young men who had stayed behind in the no-man's land in the desert on the Turkmen side of the border near the town of Takhta Bazar were being interviewed by UNHCR staff to establish why they were declining to go home.

Earlier, the International Federation of Red Cross and Rred Crescent Societies (IFRC) in the Kazakhstan capital Almaty said negotiations were under way between Afghanistan's Taleban militia and Turkmen officials on the refugees.

Bob McKerrow, head of the IFRC regional office in Almaty some 1,200 km (800 miles) from Takhta Bazar, said up to 3,000 of the refugees had gone back across the border but some later returned to Turkmenistan when they found fighting was continuing.

Mari Chak is on the Afghan side of the Murgab river, which separates Afghanistan from Turkmenistan and has been the scene of fighting between the Taleban militia and troops of northern Afghan strongman General Abdul Malik.
The Taleban are seeking to regain control of territories in the north which they briefly won but then lost in May.

Thorir Gudmundsson, regional information delegate for the IFRC, said on Thursday that 13 refugees had died in Turkmenistan, mostly from diarrhoea. The death toll had risen to 14 by Friday after a child was bitten by a snake, he said.

The refugees at Takhta Bazar were the first major influx of displaced Afghans to any of the former Soviet Central Asian states, which have often voiced fears that fighting in Afghanistan could start an exodus of civilians.
